name: Climatic Droplet Keratopathy

ethnicAssociations: Indigenous populations in arid and semi-arid regions

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical Diagnostic Criteria for Climatic Droplet Keratopathy

criteria.description: Presence of amber-colored, refractile, subepithelial corneal droplets primarily in the nasal and interpalpebral areas
History of chronic exposure to ultraviolet radiation and environmental factors such as wind and dust
Progressive stromal opacification and thinning in affected corneal regions
Lack of significant corneal inflammation or vascularization
Slit-lamp biomicroscopy revealing characteristic droplet deposits and corneal surface irregularities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic corneal droplets on slit-lamp examination with a history of chronic UV and environmental exposure, plus progressive stromal changes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical; histopathology is rarely required but shows proteinaceous deposits in Bowman’s layer and anterior stroma.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically located in the nasal and interpalpebral corneal regions

common.symptomName: Decreased visual acuity due to corneal surface irregularity
searchTerms: poor eyesight due to corneal irregularity

common.symptomName: Foreign body sensation in the eye

searchTerms: distorted vision due to cornea shape

rare.symptomName: Corneal ulceration secondary to surface breakdown

imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy showing characteristic amber-colored subepithelial droplets
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) may show hyperreflective deposits in anterior corneal layers
other: Histopathology reveals proteinaceous deposits in Bowman’s layer and anterior stroma

distinguishingFeatures: Calcium deposition in superficial cornea rather than proteinaceous droplets
Typically associated with systemic metabolic disorders or chronic inflammation
Peripheral corneal lipid deposits with gray-white arc
Usually bilateral and symmetric without amber droplets
Endothelial cell loss and corneal edema rather than subepithelial deposits

redFlags: Development of corneal ulceration or infection
Significant vision loss impacting daily activities
references: Krachmer JH, Mannis MJ, Holland EJ. Cornea. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2011.
American Academy of Ophthalmology Preferred Practice Pattern: Corneal Opacities, 2020
